42963103.titulo: Gαi3 acts as a metabolic checkpoint orchestrating TAMs immunosuppression and lipid metabolism in glucose-deprived hepatocellular carcinoma.
42963103.autores: Lu M, Li Y, Du S, Lian S, Luo J, Fang Y, Jin Y, Gao M, Wang X, Zheng M, Wang J, Xu Y, Jiang C, Jiang R
42963103.resumo:
Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are abundant in the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tumor microenvironment (TME) and undergo metabolic reprogramming to support an immunosuppressive phenotype. While G protein-coupled receptors are known sensors of environmental cues, the specific role of the inhibitory G protein subunit alpha i3 (Gαi3) in linking metabolic stress to TAMs-mediated immunosuppression remains undefined.
Clinical associations were evaluated by multiplex immunohistochemistry, Kaplan-Meier analysis, and multivariable Cox regression. Myeloid-specific Gnai3-deficient mice were studied in DEN/CCl4 or DEN/HFD-induced and orthotopic HCC models. Metabolic reprogramming was assessed by targeted metabolomics, Seahorse analysis, and pharmacological inhibition of fatty acid oxidation. Mechanistic studies included co-immunoprecipitation, a cell-free kinase assay using recombinant AMPK and Gαi3, chromatin immunoprecipitation, promoter-reporter assays, cycloheximide-chase analysis, surface-biotinylation-based EGFR recycling assays, and GBF1 knockdown/rescue experiments.
Gαi3 was upregulated in TAMs within glucose-deprived HCC regions and was associated with M2-like polarization, CD8+T cell exhaustion, and shorter overall survival. High TAM Gαi3 remained associated with overall survival after adjustment for clinical covariates. Myeloid-specific Gnai3 deletion suppressed HCC progression and restored cytotoxic CD8+T cell activity. Etomoxir phenocopied Gnai3 deficiency and attenuated macrophage-mediated T-cell suppression, supporting a requirement for fatty acid oxidation. Mechanistically, glucose deprivation activated AMPK-dependent phosphorylation of Gαi3; the cell-free kinase assay, mass spectrometry, and S143A mutagenesis together supported Ser143 as the relevant regulatory site. Active Gαi3 stabilized EGFR through a GBF1-associated trafficking program, promoted EGFR-dependent PKM2 nuclear translocation, and enhanced formation of a nuclear PKM2/HIF-1α transcriptional complex that activated Pparg and sustained an immunosuppressive fatty acid oxidation program.
Our study identifies Gαi3 as a critical metabolic checkpoint that orchestrates TAMs immunosuppression in the glucose-deprived TME. The Gαi3-EGFR-PKM2-PPARγ signaling axis drives metabolic reprogramming towards lipid oxidation, thereby inhibiting antitumor immunity. Targeting Gαi3 represents a novel immunotherapeutic strategy to reverse TAMs-mediated immunosuppression and improve outcomes in HCC.

42963011.titulo: YAP/AP-1 Activation in Sebocytes Promotes CCL5-Dependent Perifollicular Macrophage Recruitment in Rosacea.
42963011.autores: Liu J, Yang J, Zhou W, Ruan Z, Chen C, Li C, Feng C, Yan J, Liao C, Zhang H, Liu X, Cao Y, Xu D, Zhang C, Wang X, Wang P, Zeng Q
42963011.resumo: Rosacea is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder in which macrophages have been increasingly implicated, yet the spatial basis and local cues of their recruitment remain poorly defined. Given the prominent perifollicular inflammatory changes in rosacea, we investigated whether sebocytes contribute to macrophage recruitment and the underlying mechanisms. Multiplex immunofluorescence combined with distance-stratified quantification demonstrated a preferential perifollicular distribution of macrophages around pilosebaceous units (PSUs) in human rosacea lesions. Integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analyses identified the C-C motif chemokine ligand 5 (CCL5)-C-C motif chemokine receptor 5 (CCR5) axis as a candidate mediator of sebocyte-macrophage crosstalk. Silencing CCL5 by small interfering RNA and CCL5 neutralization attenuated sebocyte-driven macrophage migration in vitro and reduced macrophage accumulation in vivo. Transcriptomic analysis of sebocytes further linked CCL5 expression to activation of Yes-associated protein (YAP)/activator protein-1 (AP-1) signaling. Consistently, pharmacological inhibition of YAP or AP-1 reduced CCL5 expression in sebocytes and alleviated erythema and macrophage infiltration in vivo. Furthermore, untargeted lipidomics uncovered profound metabolic reprogramming in sebocytes, characterized notably by the accumulation of cholesteryl esters. Bidirectional interventions via simvastatin and cholesterol loading confirmed that this lipid remodeling acts as an upstream driver of YAP nuclear translocation. Overall, our study identifies a PSU-centered inflammatory niche in rosacea and implicates lipid-driven, YAP/AP-1-associated sebocytic CCL5 upregulation in perifollicular macrophage recruitment, providing a rationale for further exploring sebocyte- and pilosebaceous unit-directed therapeutic strategies in rosacea.

42962881.titulo: Targeting the Immunometabolic Checkpoint IL4I1 Suppresses the Progression of Pathological Scars.
42962881.autores: Bao Q, Huang J, Guo Y, Hu L, Li X, Tang J, Wang J, Chen X, Lu Y
42962881.resumo: Keloids are refractory fibroproliferative disorders driven by dysregulated fibrosis and chronic inflammation. Current research has largely focused on the TGF-β signaling pathway and fibroblasts-the classical drivers of keloid formation-yet clinical outcomes remain unsatisfactory. To address this, we shifted our research focus to the immunometabolic axis, with particular emphasis on the regulatory role of IL4I1 (an amino acid oxidase) as an immunometabolic checkpoint. Our results demonstrated that IL4I1 was significantly upregulated in keloid tissues, accompanied by activation of its mediated tryptophan-kynurenine metabolic pathway and increased downstream lipid peroxidation products. In vivo knockout of Il4i1 suppressed collagen deposition in a skin fibrosis model, confirming that IL4I1 plays a critical facilitatory role in fibrotic progression. We performed drug screening and identified L-carnosine as an inhibitor of IL4I1. L-carnosine inhibits the enzymatic activity and protein stability of IL4I1, and exhibits prominent therapeutic efficacy in a keloid nude-mouse xenograft model. Through its enzymatic activity, IL4I1 mediates dendritic-cell-driven immunometabolic reprogramming and the formation of an immunosuppressive microenvironment, consequently accelerating fibrotic progression. This study highlights IL4I1 as a therapeutic target, and its small-molecule inhibitor L-carnosine holds promise to be translated into a safe and clinically attractive therapeutic modality.

42962065.titulo: Integrated Metabolomic and Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals the Response Mechanisms of Phallus rubrovolvatus to Yeast Pathogen Infection.
42962065.autores: Wu P, Yuan X, Peng K, Li C, Li Y, Tarafder E, Qin Z, Tian F, Liu F
42962065.resumo: Phallus rubrovolvatus is a valuable edible and medicinal mushroom, but its cultivation is severely hindered by yellow rot disease caused by Saccharomycopsis phalli, which shows a 60 to 80% incidence and causes severe fruiting body rot, yield loss, and quality decline. The molecular mechanisms, particularly the dynamic transcriptional and metabolic responses, underlying the defense of P. rubrovolvatus against S. phalli remain poorly understood, limiting the development of targeted control strategies. To address this gap, we conducted an integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis, identifying differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially accumulated metabolites (DAMs) at 8, 16, 32, and 48 hours post-inoculation (hpi). Results showed significant changes in the pentose and glucuronate interconversion pathway, with reduced expression of related genes (e.g., ARD1, XR) and decreased accumulation of metabolites (e.g., D-glucuronic acid). Conversely, the arginine biosynthesis pathway was significantly enriched, with accumulated intermediates (e.g., citrulline, argininosuccinic acid) and upregulated biosynthesis genes (e.g., glnA, rocF). Alanine, aspartate and glutamate metabolism was also implicated in the infection response, mediating carbon-nitrogen skeleton flux and energy allocation to meet physiological demands. Additionally, glutathione metabolism was significantly enriched, accompanied by upregulated glutathione S-transferase (GST) genes. Overall, this study reveals a multi-pathway defense response in P. rubrovolvatus against S. phalli across the infection time course, involving coordinated carbon-nitrogen metabolic reprogramming and antioxidant defense activation, offering theoretical insight into its disease resistance mechanisms and supporting breeding of yellow rot-resistant varieties.

42956892.titulo: Persistent Hepatocyte Plasticity and Lipid Metabolic Reprogramming After Hepatitis C Virus Cure.
42956892.autores: Agnetti J, Cherief S, Desterke C, Bou-Malham V, Benzoubir N, Tan TZ, Thiery JP, Samuel D, Gassama-Diagne A
42956892.revista: Cellular and molecular gastroenterology and hepatology
42956892.resumo:
Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection disrupts hepatocyte polarity and promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), contributing to liver disease progression. Although direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) eradicate HCV infection in most patients, the risk of fibrosis progression and hepatocellular carcinoma persists after viral clearance. Whether antiviral cure fully restores hepatocyte differentiation, polarity, and epithelial identity programs remains unclear. We investigated whether HCV-induced EMT and lipid metabolism alterations are fully reversible following DAA treatment.
Huh7 hepatoma cells and Huh7 cells stably expressing a full-length HCV replicon were cultured in three-dimensional Matrigel to assess morphogenesis, polarity-associated features, and EMT. Spheroid morphology, canalicular-like organization, EMT markers, and transcriptomic signatures were analyzed using microscopy, immunofluorescence, RT-qPCR, and microarray analysis. The effects of DAA treatment (sofosbuvir with or without velpatasvir) were evaluated in vitro. Publicly available transcriptomic data from liver biopsies collected before therapy and within five days after its completion, were analyzed.
HCV replicon expression altered canalicular-like organization and induced actin-rich protrusions in 90% of Huh7-R spheroids. DAA treatment efficiently suppressed HCV replicon expression and partially restored epithelial morphology, reducing protrusions to 25%, without normalizing them to the control level (2.5%). EMT-associated changes, including reduced E-cadherin and increased N-cadherin expression, were only partially corrected by DAA treatment. Transcriptomic EMT scoring showed persistent mesenchymal features in DAA-treated cells and in patient biopsies collected at the end of treatment. In parallel, genes involved in lipid metabolism and hepatocyte differentiation remained dysregulated.
These findings show incomplete restoration of epithelial organization after suppression of HCV replicon expression in vitro and incomplete normalization of selected transcriptional signatures at the end of DAA treatment in patient liver samples. They suggest that cellular plasticity and metabolic reprogramming may persist after treatment and contribute to long-term liver disease risk.

42956059.titulo: Synthetic auxotrophy reveals metabolic regulation of plasma cell generation, affinity maturation, and cytokine receptor signaling.
42956059.autores: Cho SH, Brookens SK, Raybuck AL, Meyer K, Paik Y, Hamilton J, Li J, Kalecky K, Park C, Lim J, Hicks SL, Karijolich J, Bottiglieri TH, Rathmell JC, Mogilenko D, Scharer CD, Boothby MR
42956059.resumo: The proliferation and development of activated B lymphocytes into antibody (Ab)-secreting plasma cells are critical determinants of humoral immunity and sustain certain autoimmune diseases. Specific pathways and substrate supplies in intermediary metabolism influence lymphocyte differentiation and function. We now show that although stringent restriction of glutamine supply decreases B cell proliferation and differentiation into plasma cells, glutaminolysis - a major metabolic use of this amino acid - was only conditionally crucial in B cells and the Ab responses derived from them. Gls, the gene encoding the main glutaminase of lymphocytes, promoted anti-NP Ab responses at the primary and recall phases if either glucose uptake into mouse B cells or pyruvate into their mitochondria was also impaired. Otherwise, it was dispensable. This synthetic auxotrophy, that is, the conditional requirement of glutaminase for processes in addition to survival, involved supporting progressive expansion of mitochondrial respiration followed by plasma cell differentiation. Surprisingly, impairment of glutaminase and the mitochondrial pyruvate channel decreased IL-21 stimulation of STAT3 phosphorylation as well as interferon stimulation of STAT1 activation. Together, our findings establish a powerful collaboration of metabolic pathways in programming increased respiration and the development of Ab-secreting cells, but also reveal modulation of cytokine receptor signaling by metabolism.

42955323.titulo: Immunological signatures of sepsis in abdominal solid organ transplant recipients: A multilayer and multicentric prospective cohort study.
42955323.autores: Witowski A, Bracht T, Kröger L, Rump K, Nowak H, Bergmann L, Unterberg M, Rahmel T, Westhus B, Wolf A, Thon P, Ziehe D, Putensen C, Ehrentraut S, Zarbock A, Wappler F, Defosse J, Henzler D, Sitek B, Schnitzbauer A, Stervbo U, Rosiewicz K, Hugo C, Neumann S, Pagel P, Pascher A, Babel N, Adamzik M, Dyck B, Koos B
42955323.resumo:
Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction resulting from a dysregulated host response to infection. Patients with prior abdominal solid organ transplantation (SOT) are highly susceptible to infection due to chronic immunosuppression, yet exhibit improved survival once sepsis occurs. The underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.
We conducted a post hoc analysis within a prospective multicenter cohort of septic patients (SepsisDataNet.NRW; n = 538). Clinical outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. Immune profiling included serum cytokines, flow cytometric immunophenotyping, plasma proteomics, and intracellular signaling using proximity ligation assays (PLA) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). To reduce clinical confounding, complementary exploratory analyses were performed in a non-septic kidney transplant cohort (e:KID).
SOT patients demonstrated improved 30-day survival compared with non-SOT patients (84% vs. 66%; adjusted HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.95). Cytokine analysis revealed lower IL-6 and TNF-α levels alongside higher IL-18 concentrations, indicating an altered inflammatory profile. Flow cytometry showed reductions in adaptive immune cells but relatively preserved innate immune function, reflected by higher monocytic HLA-DR expression. Proteomics identified enrichment of innate immune, complement, and lipid metabolic response networks. PLA-based cellular analyses revealed increased GLUT1 expression and enhanced TFAM/TFB2M interaction in SOT patients, indicating a distinct immunometabolic marker profile. In e:KID patients paired serum metabolomics demonstrated higher glucose and lower lactate concentrations 12 months after transplantation, accompanied by broader alterations in lipid and branched-chain amino acid profiles.
In patients with sepsis, abdominal SOT is associated with significant better survival than in non-SOT patients. Septic abdominal SOT patients display a distinct immune phenotype characterized by attenuated systemic inflammation, relative preservation of selected innate immune readouts, and alterations in immunometabolic markers.

42966704.titulo: UBE2T-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming links chronic inflammation to pancreatic cancer progression.
42966704.autores: Xiao L, Ma Y, Li J, Cai W, Long B, Zhou H, Jiao Z
42966704.revista: Pancreatology : official journal of the International Association of Pancreatology (IAP) ... [et al.]
42966704.resumo:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy closely associated with chronic inflammation. However, the molecular link between persistent inflammatory signaling and lipid metabolic reprogramming during PDAC progression remains incompletely understood. We investigated the role of ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2T (UBE2T) in this process.
The effects of UBE2T were evaluated using cellular functional assays, lipidomic profiling, pathway-rescue experiments, and genetically engineered mouse models under chronic inflammatory conditions. The therapeutic effects of β-1,2,3,4,6-pentagalloylglucose (PGG), previously identified as a pharmacological inhibitor of UBE2T, were further assessed in vitro and in vivo.
Inflammatory stimulation increased UBE2T expression, whereas UBE2T depletion suppressed PDAC cell proliferation and motility- and invasion-associated phenotypes. Lipidomic analyses revealed extensive UBE2T-dependent remodeling of pancreatic lipid profiles and reduced lipid accumulation following UBE2T loss. UBE2T depletion decreased AKT phosphorylation, sterol regulatory element-binding protein (SREBP1) nuclear accumulation, and fatty acid synthase (FASN) expression. AKT activation partially rescued these alterations, whereas SREBP1 knockdown or AKT inhibition attenuated UBE2T-induced TG accumulation, supporting the involvement of the AKT/SREBP1/FASN axis. In vivo, UBE2T deficiency alleviated inflammation-associated pancreatic pathological progression and reduced pancreatic lipid accumulation. PGG treatment similarly reduced lesion burden, FASN expression, and pancreatic lipid accumulation, with concomitant attenuation of stromal remodeling.
UBE2T links chronic inflammatory signaling to AKT/SREBP1/FASN-associated lipid metabolic reprogramming during PDAC progression. UBE2T deficiency and PGG treatment attenuated pancreatic pathological progression and lipid metabolic remodeling, supporting UBE2T as a potential therapeutic target for PDAC.

42964390.titulo: Research on the molecular mechanisms and therapeutic strategies of reactive oxygen species in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
42964390.resumo: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) exhibits significant geographical clustering and etiological heterogeneity. It is particularly prevalent in Southeast Asia and is typically associated with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection. Reactive oxygen species (ROS), as highly reactive oxygen metabolites, play a key role in regulating cellular signaling and maintaining redox homeostasis. Although the role of ROS in tumors has been well established, reviews examining how ROS influence NPC and their potential therapeutic applications remain relatively scarce. ROS exert diverse effects in NPC, including roles in EBV-associated processes, regulation of programmed cell death, metabolic reprogramming, formation of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and epigenetic remodeling. In addition, natural small-molecule compounds that regulate ROS levels and emerging combination therapy strategies have considerable therapeutic potential in NPC. This review discusses the dual role of ROS in NPC, examines their contributions to disease development, and further explores how these mechanisms could inform the design of ROS-targeted therapies, as well as the associated translational challenges.

42964298.titulo: Immune microenvironment in rotator cuff healing: from macrophage dynamics to immunomodulatory regenerative therapies.
42964298.autores: Li F, Fu Z, Zhang X, Ke X, Gao X
42964298.resumo: Rotator cuff repair is increasingly limited by biology rather than fixation alone: the repaired tendon commonly heals through fibrovascular scar rather than recreating the graded tendon-fibrocartilage-bone enthesis, particularly in aging, metabolic disease, muscle degeneration, and poor bone quality. The immune microenvironment is a dynamic determinant of whether injury progresses toward persistent inflammation and fibrosis or toward resolution and regeneration. This Review synthesizes immune regulation across the rotator cuff muscle-tendon-enthesis-bone unit, with emphasis on macrophage heterogeneity, efferocytosis, autophagy, immunometabolism, mechanosensing, and immune-stromal crosstalk. Human single-cell studies identify pro-fibrotic macrophage, senescent tenocyte, osteopontin/TGF-beta, and endothelial programs in rotator cuff scar, while mechanistic studies nominate resolution pathways as therapeutic targets. We critically evaluate cytokine/chemokine modulation, extracellular vesicles, senomorphic strategies, bioactive ions, ROS-responsive materials, nanoengineered interfaces, and rehabilitation-based immunomodulation. Across these approaches, the key translational requirements are causal mechanism, validation in chronic or aged disease models and human tissue, integration of structural and mechanical outcomes, arthroscopic deployability, manufacturing feasibility, and biomarker-guided patient selection. Together, these data support a shift from nonspecific anti-inflammatory augmentation toward mechanism-based, pro-resolution strategies for durable tendon-to-bone repair.

42959951.titulo: Integrated multi-omics reveals gut microbiota-metabolic mechanisms underlying the neuroprotective effects of Xijiao Dihuang Decoction against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
42959951.autores: Long YY, Feng YJ, Mao KN, Song ZG, Liu YC, Chen SY, Zheng CX, Zeng YD, Yin ST, Dai SS, Li H, Liu WH
42959951.resumo:
Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) remains a major barrier to functional recovery after reperfusion therapy for ischemic stroke. Increasing evidence indicates that gut microbiota dysbiosis and metabolic disturbance are closely involved in post-stroke neuroinflammation and secondary brain injury. Xijiao Dihuang Decoction (XDD), a classical traditional Chinese medicine formula, has shown protective effects in cerebrovascular disorders; however, whether its effects against CIRI are associated with coordinated regulation of the gut microbiota and host metabolism remains unclear.
Circulating XDD-derived components were characterized by ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). Network pharmacology and molecular docking were used to predict potential targets and signaling pathways associated with CIRI. A middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) rat model was established, and rats were treated with low-, medium-, or high-dose XDD for 7 days, with edaravone as a positive control. Neurological deficits, cerebral infarct volume, hemorheological parameters, histopathological changes, and serum inflammatory cytokines were assessed. Cecal microbiota composition was analyzed by 16S rDNA sequencing, and cecal metabolic profiles were investigated using untargeted LC-MS metabolomics. Multi-omics integration and Spearman correlation analysis were performed to explore associations between differentially abundant bacterial genera and characteristic metabolites.
A total of 54 XDD-derived circulating components were identified. Network pharmacology analysis indicated that the putative targets of XDD were mainly enriched in pathways related to inflammation, lipid and energy metabolism, and regulated cell death, with AKT1 and NLRP3 were predicted as potential hub targets. In MCAO/R rats, XDD improved neurological deficits, reduced cerebral infarct volume, alleviated hemorheological abnormalities, and attenuated neuronal injury. XDD also reduced serum IL-6 levels and lowered IL-1β levels mainly at medium and high doses. In addition, XDD partially restored gut microbial diversity and remodeled CIRI-associated microbial dysbiosis. Metabolomics analysis revealed marked metabolic disturbances after MCAO/R, and XDD reversed part of these alterations, particularly those related to lipid metabolism. Integrated analysis further linked specific bacterial genera with lipid mediators and fatty acid-related metabolites, indicating coordinated remodeling of the gut microbiota and host metabolism.
XDD exerts neuroprotective effects against CIRI through multi-target and multi-pathway actions. Its therapeutic effects may be associated with coordinated regulation of gut microbial homeostasis, metabolic reprogramming, and inflammatory/cell death signaling. These findings provide new evidence supporting the potential application of XDD in ischemic stroke and offer insight into microbiota-related mechanisms underlying its neuroprotective effects.

42959626.titulo: Research progress of mitophagy and its targeted therapeutic strategies in rheumatoid arthritis.
42959626.autores: Zhang Y, Ge F, Wang X
42959626.resumo: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic, systemic autoimmune inflammatory disease characterized by persistent joint inflammation and progressive bone destruction. In recent years, mitophagy-a selective form of autophagy-has garnered increasing attention. As a critical cellular process, mitophagy specifically removes damaged mitochondria and maintains mitochondrial homeostasis and energy metabolic balance. Accumulating evidence suggests that mitophagy not only regulates cell survival and metabolic reprogramming but also plays a central role in preserving immune homeostasis, modulating immune cell polarization, and suppressing inflammatory signaling. This article reviews the molecular mechanisms of mitophagy and its pivotal role in RA, along with recent advances in mitophagy-targeted therapeutic strategies, aiming to provide novel insights for RA treatment.

42963430.titulo: Cholesterol binding stabilizes the activated state of THIK-1 and promotes atherosclerosis.
42963430.autores: Dai Z, Li Y, Hou Z, Duan G, Hu Z, Yang A, Wang Q, Wang W, Luo J, Zuo P, Yin Y, Yin Y
42963430.resumo: Atherosclerosis, a chronic inflammatory disorder, remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality. While cholesterol is known to activate the NLRP3-IL-1β pathway and promote plaque formation, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify the tandem pore domain halothane-inhibited potassium channel 1 (THIK-1) as a mediator of IL-1β release during atherosclerosis progression. Using high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), we determine the structure of THIK-1 in its apo form and in complex with the activator arachidonic acid, and the inhibitors halothane and C101248 as well as the structure of the disease-related THIK-1 R92S variant. Structural analyses reveal that cholesterol unexpectedly stabilizes the arachidonic acid-binding pocket within THIK-1. Complementary cellular assays confirm that cholesterol amplifies the arachidonic acid-induced inflammatory response in macrophages, which can be effectively suppressed by the THIK-1 inhibitors halothane and C101248. Moreover, treatment with C101248 markedly reduces atherosclerotic plaque development in Apoe-deficient mice fed a high-cholesterol diet. Collectively, these findings elucidate a cholesterol-dependent mechanism of THIK-1 regulation and highlight THIK-1 as a regulator of atherosclerosis.

42962025.titulo: Cryo-EM structure of a protein nanopore reveals lipid acyl chains as integral components.
42962025.autores: Ashworth M, Noble OW, Plevin MJ, Bayfield OW, Antson AA
42962025.resumo: Nanopore-based technologies are revolutionizing nucleic acid sequencing and molecular sensing, yet the structural basis by which pore-forming proteins interact with lipid membranes remains poorly defined. The mycobacterial porin MspA is a benchmark biological nanopore owing to its exceptional stability and uniquely narrow constriction, but accurate structural information is limited to protein-only models. Here, we present a 2.5-angstrom resolution cryo-electron microscopy structure of the M2 mutant of MspA embedded in a phospholipid nanodisc, providing a high-resolution experimental observation of MspA in a lipid environment. The structure reveals an annular arrangement of extended lipid acyl chains surrounding the MspA oligomer and contacting the transmembrane barrel. Their resolved densities indicate a substantially more ordered annular lipid environment than would be expected from a largely heterogeneous and nonspecific protein-lipid interface. The structure also demonstrates how specific M2 MspA mutations modulate pore polarity, influencing ion selectivity and transport. By determining the membrane-embedded structure of MspA and revealing an ordered arrangement of acyl chains forming extensive hydrophobic interactions with the protein, this study demonstrates the importance of the surrounding lipid environment in the design of protein nanopores.

42958045.titulo: First report of culturable fungi associated with the Brazilian sharpnose shark (Rhizoprionodon lalandii) from southeastern Brazil.
42958045.autores: Oliveira MME, da Costa GL, de Souza BA, de Oliveira Baptista B, Barbosa BF, Hauser-Davis RA
42958045.resumo:
Climate change and other anthropogenic environmental changes may alter fungal distributions and ecological interactions, potentially facilitating the emergence or redistribution of opportunistic fungi in marine ecosystems. These shifts raise concerns regarding microbial contamination in seafood and the need for surveillance in marine organisms. Elasmobranchs, such as sharks and rays, are ecologically and economically important but remain understudied regarding fungal occurrence in wild populations. This study provides the first report of cultivable fungal taxa associated with the Brazilian sharpnose shark (Rhizoprionodon lalandii) from southeastern Brazil.
Swabs from the mouth, gills, and cloaca were obtained from 22 specimens procured from artisanal fisheries in Cabo Frio, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Fungal occurrence varied among sampled anatomical sites and individuals, with several cloacal samples showing abundant growth under the culture conditions employed. Recovered isolates consisted primarily of members of the Candida parapsilosis species complex and Meyerozyma guilliermondii, alongside occasional detection of other yeast taxa including Rhodotorula mucilaginosa, Debaryomyces hansenii, Trichosporon japonicum, and Pichia terricola. Because fungal recovery relied on culture-based methods, ITS sequencing of representative colonies, and sampling restricted to external and cloacal tissues, the detected assemblage likely reflects predominant culturable taxa rather than total fungal diversity. Furthermore, implications for food safety, transmission pathways, or environmental contamination remain speculative and warrant targeted investigation.
These findings expand current knowledge regarding fungi associated with R. lalandii and highlight the need for additional studies incorporating environmental sampling, edible tissue analyses, and broader fungal characterization approaches to better understand potential ecological and public health implications.

42964622.titulo: Breaking the degenerative triad: Microenvironment reprogramming biomaterials for intervertebral disc regeneration.
42964622.autores: Zhao X, Han X, Hu Z, Chen Y, Wang X, Liu Q, Hu X, Zhang Q, Yue J, Ge Y, Ma Y, Li Y, Zhang Z, Li F, Chen W, Zhang Y
42964622.resumo: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) represents a leading cause of chronic low back pain worldwide, imposing considerable public health and socioeconomic burdens. Current clinical interventions remain largely palliative, unable to reverse the progressive pathological cascade. This cascade is driven by a core self-amplifying triad of oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and nutrient deprivation within the unique avascular, high-load disc niche, and ultimately progresses to end-stage terminal phenotypes such as biomechanical failure and neurovascular ingrowth. Over recent years, biomaterial-based regenerative strategies have evolved from passive structural fillers toward multifunctional platforms capable of active microenvironmental reprogramming. This review provides a systematic, critical synthesis of state-of-the-art advances in the field, organized within a hierarchical framework spanning immunometabolic modulation of the degenerative niche and targeted delivery of cellular and molecular therapeutics with further elaboration of precision-stratified design and whole-disc tissue engineering. We critically appraise evidence maturity across different strategy classes and dissect disc-specific translational barriers, noting that most candidate platforms remain at preclinical validation stages. Building on this analysis, we outline priority research directions and realistic near-term translational milestones to guide rational development of next-generation regenerative platforms toward durable functional disc repair.

42960458.titulo: Mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives of mucosal glycosylation-innate immunity crosstalk in inflammatory bowel disease (Review).
42960458.autores: Liu X, Zhang T, Jin J, Song Y, Li M, Zhong H, Cai M, Ding S, Han X
42960458.resumo: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a group of chronic, relapsing inflammatory disorders of the gastrointestinal tract, driven by a complex interplay of genetic susceptibility, environmental exposures, intestinal microbiota dysbiosis and immune dysregulation. In recent years, mucosal glycosylation has emerged as a fundamental molecular determinant of intestinal barrier integrity and function and is increasingly recognized as a key regulatory interface linking the microbiota with host immune responses. Concurrently, the innate immune system serves an important role in mucosal defense and inflammatory responses through pattern recognition receptor‑mediated signaling, and its aberrant activation represents a key driver of persistent inflammation in IBD. The present review systematically summarizes the bidirectional regulatory crosstalk between mucosal glycosylation and innate immunity. The mechanistic roles of glycosylation modifications are highlighted in pathogen recognition, inflammatory signal transduction, inflammasome activation and maintenance of mucosal barrier integrity. Conversely, it is discussed how innate immune activation regulates glycan biosynthesis and remodeling through inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress and major signaling pathways, thereby reshaping the mucosal glycome in disease contexts. On this basis, the dynamic alterations of glycosylation‑innate immunity interactions across different stages of IBD, including disease initiation, progression and relapse, are delineated, emphasizing their important role in sustaining chronic inflammation and driving tissue remodeling. In addition, emerging therapeutic strategies targeting glycosylation pathways, glycan‑lectin interactions, mucosal barrier restoration and microbiota modulation are summarized. The potential of glycomics, multi‑omics integration and glyco‑immune biomarkers in disease stratification and precision medicine are also discussed. By integrating perspectives from glycobiology and immunology, the present review aims to provide a conceptual framework and novel directions for mechanistic research and targeted therapy in IBD.

42953735.titulo: Spatiotemporally coordinated immunometabolic-hyperthermia therapy for diabetic bone defect regeneration.
42953735.autores: Wang L, Peng X, Zheng L, Liu Y, Chen L, Li X, Wang Z
42953735.resumo: Diabetic bone defects (DBDs) are typified by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, and microbial infection within the diabetic microenvironment, which collectively hinder osteogenesis and angiogenesis. Herein, we introduce an Immunometabolic-Hyperthermia Therapy (IMHT) strategy based on a dual-functional nanoplatform, namely a polydopamine/itaconate-incorporated agarose/gelatin (PIAG) hydrogel. This system is fabricated by incorporating itaconic acid (ITA) into polydopamine (PDA) nanoparticles through in situ polymerization, followed by encapsulation within a gelatin/agarose matrix. ITA primarily provides immunometabolic regulation, while PDA enables a tunable photothermal response. Upon localized photothermal heating (∼50 °C), the PIAG hydrogel effectively disrupts bacterial biofilms, with photothermal treatment providing the dominant antibacterial effect and ITA offering an additional supportive contribution. Upon mild photothermal activation (∼41 °C), IMHT mitigates excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, inhibits neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, and reprograms macrophages toward an M2-like reparative phenotype through JAK1/STAT1 pathway inhibition. The resulting pro-regenerative immune milieu enhances fibroblast growth factor-2 (FGF-2) secretion, while heat-induced activation of HSP90 stabilizes FGF-2/FGFR1 signaling, further promoting osteogenic differentiation and endothelial migration. Overall, the spatiotemporally coordinated antibacterial, immunometabolic, and regenerative regulation realized by IMHT offers a comprehensive and effective strategy for the repair of diabetic bone defects.

42969658.titulo: Deciphering Host Genomic Pathway Landscapes in Severe COVID-19 by Exome Sequencing of a Large Admixed Brazilian Cohort.
42969658.autores: Zetum ASS, Silva DRCD, Ventorim VDP, Mion FA, Passarela FDS, Brasil P, Campos TL, Acioli-Santos B, Oliveira FRDS, Trabach RSDR, Altoé LSC, Meira DD, Louro ID
42969658.resumo: The host genetic factors that resulted in the heterogeneous clinical outcomes of COVID-19 remained poorly understood, especially in admixed populations that are underrepresented in global genomic studies. In this study, we investigated the genetic landscape associated with COVID-19 severity using whole-exome sequencing data from 325 Brazilian individuals recruited between 2020 and 2023. To prioritize variants related to disease severity, we applied a machine learning framework combining Support Vector Machine - Recursive Feature Elimination and SHAP interpretation. This approach encompasses 25 variants that contributed to the model's discrimination between severe and non-severe cases (AUC = 0.94) in our cohort. Subsequently, logistic regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, principal components of ancestry, and significant comorbidities confirmed several loci associated with severity after correction for multiple testing (FDR < 0.05). The prioritized genes were grouped into biological axes, including mitochondrial bioenergetics, neuroimmune signaling, complement activation, and epithelial structural integrity. Variants in genes such as MUC16, SLC4A2, LAPS1, ARRDC2, and CCSER1 showed associations with disease severity. Furthermore, functional annotation using CADD and regulatory exploration using GTEx suggested that several loci may influence gene regulation in lung, immune, and neural tissues. Instead of implicating single causal variants, our findings highlight pathway-level genetic architectures that may contribute to the variability of the host response to COVID-19. These findings provide exploratory insights into potential host genetic pathways that may be involved in disease variability in admixed environments. However, replication in independent cohorts and functional validation are still needed.

42952152.titulo: Macrophage GLUD1 is Essential for Redox Balance and Immune Homeostasis in Cardiac Injury.
42952152.autores: Jin T, Lai C, Zhou Q, Wang R, Tong Y, Chen W, Rabrenovic N, Zhang T, Ren X, Huang C, Chen J, Li R, Yu L, Mazzone M, Zhang W, Fu G, Shang M
42952152.resumo: Excessive free radical production and dysregulated immune responses contribute to myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury. However, the mechanisms by which macrophages regulate reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis and orchestrate immune responses during IR injury remain elusive. Here, we show that glutamate dehydrogenase 1 (GLUD1) expression is induced in monocytes from patients with acute myocardial infarction after interventional therapy and in cardiac-recruited macrophages from mice subjected to IR injury. GLUD1-deficient macrophages exacerbate IR injury by increasing mitochondrial ROS accumulation and amplifying pro-inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, GLUD1 deficiency leads to mitochondrial ROS accumulation due to reduced NADPH/NADP+ and GSH/GSSG ratios during IR injury. Elevated mitochondrial ROS inhibits PHD2 activity, stabilizing HIF-1α and enhancing NF-κB signaling, promoting the release of pro-inflammatory factors and exacerbating myocardial damage. Systemic activation of GLUD1 or adoptive transfer of monocytes pre-treated with a GLUD1 activator preserved cardiac function and mitigated IR injury. These findings highlight macrophage GLUD1 as a critical regulator of redox balance and immune homeostasis, presenting a promising therapeutic target for alleviating IR injury and preserving cardiac function.

42964061.titulo: Targeting TLR4 alleviates the progression of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis by regulating central resident cells and Th1/Th17 cell differentiation.
42964061.autores: Du E, Lei K, Deng W, Yang S, Liu Y, Dai J, Lei J, Zhang R, Tao H, Chen H, Sun Y
42964061.resumo: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease characterized by neuroinflammation. Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) is a receptor for damage-associated molecular patterns, such as high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) and plays a role in innate immunity. However, its precise role and cellular dynamics in MS pathogenesis are unclear. Using the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) model, we mapped the expression dynamics of TLR4 and found that in the spinal cords, the cell type associated with the disease shifted from neurons to activated glia. To establish causality, we subjected TLR4 -/- mice to EAE and observed significantly attenuated disease severity, reduced demyelination, and preserved neuronal integrity, alongside suppressed microglial and astrocytic activation. Furthermore, TLR4 deficiency was not merely dampening CNS-localized inflammation but was also associated with suppressed peripheral MOG35-55-specific Th1/Th17 effector responses, as evidenced by reduced production of IFN-γ and IL-17A in lymphoid organs, together with reduced TNF-α, as well as diminished expression of the Th1/Th17 lineage-defining transcription factors T-bet and RORγt in the spinal cord infiltrates. This suggests that TLR4 plays a key role in EAE pathology by connecting peripheral Th1/Th17 differentiation with central glial inflammatory responses. Critically, to translate these findings, we evaluated the small-molecule TLR4 antagonist TAK-242. While prophylactic administration was effective, therapeutic dosing initiated after disease onset still significantly alleviated clinical scores and delayed progression, highlighting its potential for clinical intervention. Overall, our results demonstrate that targeting TLR4 simultaneously curtails pathogenic T-cell differentiation and local neuroinflammation, establishing TLR4 as a dual-action therapeutic target for MS.

42969843.titulo: 3D Electron Diffraction Reveals Counterion Coordination in Co-Existing Polymorphs of Ag29 Nanocluster.
42969843.autores: Nagar H, Gurung K, Kučeráková M, Som A, Palatinus L, Pradeep T
42969843.resumo: We unravel the complete structural architecture of the polymorphic Na3[Ag29(BDT)12(TPP)4] nanocluster (NC) using three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) of microscopic crystals. By drop-casting nanocluster solution directly onto microscopy grids, we achieve in situ crystallization of nanometer-sized polymorphs and independently resolve co-existing cubic and trigonal phases crystal-by-crystal from a single grid square. Using difference electrostatic potential (DESP) maps derived from empirical 3D ED data, we pinpoint the specific lattice locations of the elusive Na+ counterions and observe distinct coordination environments across the two polymorphs. In the densely packed, solvent-free cubic phase, Na+ binds exclusively to thermodynamically favored pockets formed by one core-anchored and two staple sulfur atoms. Conversely, within the open, solvated trigonal lattice, Na+ occupies both these core-anchored sites and alternative positions coordinated entirely by three sulfur atoms of an outer Ag3S3 staple motif. These findings establish 3D ED as a powerful tool for resolving nanoscale polymorphic mixtures and demonstrate how macroscopic crystal packing influences local ionic interactions, providing key structural insights for the design of cluster-based assemblies.

42968263.titulo: An evaluation framework for sparse 4D (3D + time) imaging reconstruction via bootstrapped cross-validation.
42968263.autores: Zhang Y, Yao Z, Hu Z, Ritschel T, Villanueva-Perez P
42968263.resumo: Four-dimensional (4D; 3D + time) microscopic imaging has emerged as a powerful technique for investigating dynamic phenomena in complex systems, enabling direct visualisation of structural evolution in space and time. However, when pushing the limits of spatiotemporal resolution, most time-resolved imaging techniques yield inherently sparse 4D datasets. While deep learning-based reconstruction methods have shown promise in reconstructing 4D from sparse spatiotemporal measurements, a practical approach for evaluating their performance in the absence of a 4D reference has, to the best of our knowledge, been lacking. Here, we present a bootstrapped cross-validation framework that estimates reconstruction performance by quantifying correlations between reconstructions generated from independently sampled subsets of the acquired data, as inspired by the 3D validation strategy in cryo-electron microscopy, where reconstructions from split datasets are compared to assess resolutions. This enables both qualitative and quantitative assessment in the absence of ground truth. We investigate two representative scenarios with sparse and ultra-sparse X-ray datasets and validate this approach using 4D-ONIX, a 4D deep-learning reconstruction method, on simulated water droplet collision experiments. The proposed approach provides a reference-free framework for performance estimation and support for better-informed experimental strategies across a wide range of ultrafast imaging applications.

42963474.titulo: "Frozen" chromatin: insights on its structuring from cryo-EM tomography.
42963474.autores: Golyshev S, Kazakov E, Kireev I
42963474.revista: Chromosome research : an international journal on the molecular, supramolecular and evolutionary aspects of chromosome biology
42963474.resumo: Chromatin is a DNA-protein polymer that ensures the safekeeping and realization of genetic information in eukaryotic cells. The genome of higher eukaryotes is packed into a relatively small nuclear volume and organized in a non-random yet non-deterministic manner, exhibiting a high degree of complexity and flexibility. Despite the dense packing of chromatin, the cell effectively controls transcription, replication, and DNA repair. Genomic approaches, direct visualization, and computer modeling have allowed to accumulate a large amount of data on the structure and behavior of chromatin in various functional states. However, many of these techniques rely on chemical cross-linking, membrane permeabilization, or altered ionic conditions, which may perturb native chromatin structure. This has led to contradictory views on chromatin organization in situ. Cryo-electron microscopy (Cryo-EM) ensures preservation of the cellular structures in a close to native hydrated state and provides high resolving power, thus becoming a tool of choice for studying organization of chromatin at the nucleosomal and supranucleosomal scales. This review summarizes how cryo-EM has advanced our understanding of chromatin organization and function, considers the limitations of the method, and discusses future directions and perspectives in the field.

42963453.titulo: EMC chaperone activity is required for cotranslational calcium channel assembly.
42963453.autores: Stanton M, Scheuing CE, Biswal M, Singal B, Agarwal M, Vargas GD, Gao A, Brademan DR, Hüttenhain R, Gifford CA, Pleiner T
42963453.resumo: Nearly half of the ~5,000 human membrane proteins need to assemble into stoichiometric complexes as part of their biogenesis at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane. How ER-resident biogenesis factors coordinate membrane insertion, folding and assembly is not well understood. Here we demonstrate that the human ER membrane protein complex (EMC) insertase additionally acts as a chaperone to facilitate the assembly of heterotrimeric voltage-gated calcium channels (Cav). Using function-separating mutations and inhibitory nanobodies, we show that nascent Cav channels are degraded prematurely when EMC's chaperone function is selectively perturbed. Blocking EMC's chaperone function impaired Cav-dependent cardiomyocyte contraction. EMC engagement of the pore-forming Cav α-subunit occurred cotranslationally and required the Cav α-subunit's first transmembrane domain bundle to protrude from the nascent ribosome-multipass translocon complex. Our findings establish a chaperone function for the EMC and suggest that biogenesis of multibundle membrane proteins may require a highly orchestrated, cotranslational interplay among ER biogenesis factors.

42963376.titulo: A multimeric pore complex in the poxvirus core revealed by integrative structural analysis.
42963376.autores: Liu J, Schäfer S, Lehnung S, Baumann LM, Mühlberg L, Steiner C, Schreiber M, Linder M, Welsch S, Liu F, Bogdanow B, Krijnse Locker J, Turoňová B
42963376.resumo: It has long been known that poxviruses transcribe more than a hundred early mRNAs within their viral core, yet how these transcripts exit the core remains unknown. Here, we combine cryo-electron tomography with deep-learning-based particle picking, subtomogram averaging, cross-linking mass spectrometry, and AlphaFold3 modeling to resolve the molecular architecture of a long-sought pore within the poxvirus core. The pore is formed by a heteromeric assembly of the viral proteins E8, E6, and L3, which together create a hollow hexameric tube spanning both the core wall and the surface-exposed palisade layer. Within the pore channel, we observe a rod-like density consistent with the viral RNA helicase I8, which may contribute to the release of the newly synthesized viral mRNAs from the core. We further observe a state of the pore lacking the outer and basal rings under transcription conditions. Together, our findings identify the structure and dynamics of a candidate mRNA-release pore within the surface layer of a double-stranded DNA virus and suggest that it may form part of the poxvirus transcription machinery.

42956544.titulo: The dynamics of large biomolecular assemblies.
42956544.autores: Wanes G, Ding E, Onuchic JN, Whitford PC
42956544.resumo: With recent advances in cryo-electron microscopy/cryo-electron tomography (cryoEM/cryoET), computational capabilities and machine learning, there has been an incredible increase in the speed of structure determination for large biomolecular assemblies. In order to connect these static descriptions with biological function, one needs reliable and accurate approaches to quantify the factors that regulate dynamics. For this, models that employ simplified energetics and/or coarse-grained representations have become indispensable tools for integrating structural insights, biochemical analyses and physical principles. Here we discuss examples where molecular simulations have provided a framework for understanding dynamics in assemblies of increasing size and complexity. We focus on three classes for which there have been notable advances in recent years: ribosomes, viral capsids and nuclear pore complexes. Each possesses unique physical attributes that have required distinct theoretical and computational strategies. Together, these studies provide a rich conceptual and technical foundation that can help shape our perspective on the machinery of the cell.

42955953.titulo: Molecular insights into the activation mechanism of the slow anion channel AtSLAH3.
42955953.autores: Wang Y, Zhao B, Pan D, He F, Wang S, Liu J, Peng M, Sun H, Zhou X, Liu L, Yao X, Gao S
42955953.resumo: The plant slow anion channel SLAH3 regulates essential physiological processes, including stomatal closure and stress responses, yet the structural mechanism underlying its activation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the activation mechanism of SLAH3 by determining cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of the wild-type (WT) channel and gain-of-function mutants identified through a targeted mutagenesis screen of pore-lining residues. Notably, the L400A mutant was captured in a dilated, open-like conformation, in contrast to the auto-inhibited WT channel. Structural comparisons revealed concerted rearrangements of the pore-lining transmembrane helices and intracellular regulatory elements. The observations point to an activation model in which displacement of the intracellular auto-inhibitory module relieves pore occlusion, triggering conformational changes that propagate from the intracellular loop to pore-lining segments, ultimately widening the entrance for anion transport. Therefore, our study provides a structural framework for understanding SLAH3 regulation and advances our understanding of nitrate signaling and stress adaptation in plants.

42955944.titulo: Antibody 3CF5 neutralizes historical and emerging H5Nx influenza viruses by targeting a conserved non-receptor-binding hemagglutinin epitope.
42955944.autores: Liang H, Niu C, Cheng Y, Liew KY, Qu L, Zheng Z, Yang W, Wang Q, Wei L, Liu B, Hu F, Xing C, Chen J, Pan W, Li P, Tan YJ, Xiong X, Chen L, Niu X
42955944.resumo: Avian influenza viruses of the H5Nx subtype pose persistent pandemic threats. Here, we immunized rhesus macaques with an H5N6 vaccine and obtained 30 H5-reactive monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). Three IgG mAbs, 3CF5, 3BG3, and 3BE7, demonstrated potent neutralizing activity against multiple H5Nx viruses and conferred protection in a lethal mouse challenge model. Notably, 3CF5 exhibited broad neutralization against H5Nx viruses spanning 1997-2024, including contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 strains associated with an ongoing outbreak in dairy cattle. Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) analysis revealed that 3CF5 targets a conserved non-receptor-binding epitope on the hemagglutinin (HA) head, spanning the vestigial esterase domain and an adjacent lateral surface. 3CF5 mediates neutralization primarily through inhibiting membrane fusion and also possesses antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. Furthermore, isotype conversion of 3CF5-IgG to mucosal secretory IgA1 (sIgA1) enhanced neutralization potency against H5N1 viruses up to 128-fold, highlighting the advantage of sIgA1 as a nasally administered prophylactic agent.

42951937.titulo: Structural mechanism of programmable gene integration by the R2 retrotransposon coupled with CRISPR-Cas9.
42951937.autores: Komatsu D, Hiraizumi M, Fell CW, Fujimatsu K, Nagahata N, Yamada S, Sapkota S, Ramani H, Arya B, Shibata M, Yamashita K, Gootenberg JS, Abudayyeh OO, Nishimasu H
42951937.resumo: R2 retroelements are non-long-terminal-repeat retrotransposons that primarily insert into 28S ribosomal DNA loci across diverse eukaryotes. R2 elements home to their target sites through target-primed reverse transcription (TPRT), in which the R2 protein recognizes and nicks the target DNA to prime reverse transcription using an R2-encoding RNA as the template. The avian R2 system from Taeniopygia guttata (R2Tg) can insert a payload sequence within an RNA template into 28S ribosomal DNA loci in human cells. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy structures of the R2Tg-template RNA-target DNA complex in the TPRT initiation state, both alone and bound to a Cas9-guide RNA complex. These structures provide mechanistic insights into R2Tg-mediated TPRT in its natural context and in the programmable gene integration system STITCHR (site-specific target-primed insertion through targeted CRISPR homing of retroelements). Furthermore, we combine these structural insights with computational protein design methods to engineer an enhanced STITCHR system.

42959586.titulo: Deep Learning for Protein Secondary-Structure Segmentation in Intermediate-Resolution Cryo-EM Maps: A Resolution-Stratified Benchmark Dataset and Controlled Evaluation.
42959586.autores: Pial MER, Dehan FN, Sazzed S
42959586.resumo: Accurate segmentation of protein secondary structures in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) maps is crucial for protein tracing and atomic model building, yet remains challenging at intermediate resolutions. Although deep learning architectures have recently been applied to this task, there remains a lack of standardized evaluation protocols and systematic resolution-stratified analyses. Consequently, it remains unclear how segmentation performance varies across finer resolution ranges within the intermediate-resolution regime and how different volumetric segmentation architectures compare under controlled experimental conditions. To address these gaps, we present a nonredundant, resolution-stratified benchmark dataset and a controlled evaluation framework for protein secondary-structure segmentation in intermediate-resolution cryo-EM maps. The dataset comprises 972 nonredundant protein-chain samples from 495 cryo-EM protein structures resolved at 4.5-8.0 Å, with voxel-level annotations for helices, sheets, and non-periodic secondary-structure (NPSS) regions. The dataset is stratified into three resolution ranges4.5-5.5, 5.5-6.5, and 6.5-8.0 Åto enable systematic analysis of resolution-dependent segmentation performance. Using this benchmark, we evaluate five representative convolutional and transformer-based volumetric segmentation architecturesU-Net, Residual U-Net, Attention U-Net, UNETR, and Swin-UNETRunder standardized preprocessing, training, and evaluation protocols. Residual U-Net achieves the highest macro-averaged foreground (Macro-FG) F1 score in all three resolution bins, while helices are segmented more accurately than sheets and NPSS regions. All five architectures achieve their highest Macro-FG F1 scores in the highest-resolution bin, whereas performance varies between the two lower-resolution bins across architectures and secondary-structure classes. Overall, this benchmark enables fine-grained analysis of resolution-dependent segmentation performance, supports reproducible method development, and facilitates controlled comparison of future cryo-EM secondary-structure segmentation approaches.

42959064.titulo: A learning-to-rank framework for large-scale identification of unknown proteins from cryo-EM and cryo-ET maps.
42959064.revista: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
42959064.resumo: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) can yield density maps whose molecular identities are unknown. Predicted-structure databases enable proteome-scale searches, but distinguishing the correct candidates remains challenging, particularly for intermediate-resolution maps without clear side-chain features. We developed CryoAssign, an automated framework that combines large-scale structure matching with learning-to-rank prioritization. CryoAssign searches intact density maps without prior segmentation and integrates complementary measures of map-model agreement. On held-out benchmark maps, CryoAssign robustly prioritized the correct candidates. It also identified proteins or narrowed the set of candidates in previously unassigned cryo-EM maps and recovered multiple components from complex cryo-EM and cryo-ET maps. Controlled low-pass filtering showed generally robust recovery across a broad range of intermediate resolutions. CryoAssign provides a scalable approach for identifying proteins from cryo-EM and cryo-ET density maps.

42963108.titulo: Conservation of a synaptic blueprint across the animal kingdom.
42963108.resumo: Chemical synapses are fundamental computational units of the nervous system that enable rapid and precise information transfer through the nanoscale organization of presynaptic and postsynaptic components. Despite hundreds of millions of years of animal evolution and extraordinary diversity in nervous system architectures, the core physiological principles of chemical synaptic transmission remain remarkably conserved. Studies across Drosophila melanogaster, zebrafish, Caenorhabditis elegans, frogs and mammals reveal recurring principles governing active-zone organization, synaptic vesicle exocytosis, calcium signalling and postsynaptic specialization. Here, we examine the evolution of chemical synapses across the animal kingdom, focusing on the relationship between molecular diversification, nanoscale organization and functional conservation. We propose that the evolutionary stability of synapses reflects, in part, a stringent biophysical constraint imposed by the requirements for rapid chemical communication. We further consider how these conserved synaptic operations are assembled into neural circuits of dramatically different complexities, as well as the ctenophore nervous system as a critical test case for distinguishing molecular conservation from architectural and functional convergence. Across species, the emerging picture is that evolution has adhered to conserving the geometry and organizational principles of chemical synapses more stringently than a precise molecular composition. Synapses thus represent stable yet adaptable information-processing architectures in which conserved nanoscale constraints coexist with molecular flexibility and extensive diversification of neural circuits.

42958608.titulo: Advances in research on the regulation of honey bee odor and chemical communication by symbiotic microorganisms.
42958608.autores: Chen YJ, Wang YC, Pang YT, Fang RC, Zhang J, Ke XH, Li JJ, Zhang LS, Yang S, Guo J, Miao CH
42958608.resumo: Because honey bees are key pollinators in terrestrial ecosystems, they are highly sensitive to environmental changes, and colony survival serves as a reliable indicator of environmental conditions. Insect symbiotic microorganisms regulate host chemical communication through multiple pathways, thereby playing critical roles in pheromone synthesis, olfactory perception, and social behavior modulation. However, a systematic review of the potential regulatory mechanisms by which symbiotic microorganisms influence chemical communication in honey bees is still lacking. Here, we synthesize domestic and international research to assess the compositions of symbiotic microorganisms in honey bees, as well as the mechanisms of pheromone release, perception, and function. Furthermore, drawing on specific experimental cases, we discuss how honey bee symbionts modulate host sensitivity to chemical signals and consequently affect host social behavior through multiple routes. These pathways are involved in regulating odorant-binding protein or odorant receptor expression and nervous system function, altering cuticular hydrocarbon profiles, modulating olfactory memory, and mediating immune signaling. This review further explores the interplay between symbiotic microorganisms and the release and reception of chemical signals in honey bees, thereby providing a solid foundation for the conservation of endangered pollinating insects.

42957805.titulo: Olfactory differences among cactophilic Drosophila species.
42957805.autores: Hamrick A, Layne JE, Lawson LP, Solomon N, Rollmann SM
42957805.revista: Journal of comparative physiology. A, Neuroethology, sensory, neural, and behavioral physiology
42957805.resumo: Divergence of behavioral traits with adaptation to changes in the environment has been well documented in many animals and is often accompanied by divergence in sensory systems. Shifts in insect host plant preference behavior, in particular, are often associated with changes to the olfactory system, including differences in the sensitivity, specificity, or abundance of olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs). Here, we examine 12 species from the cactophilic Drosophila repleta group that represent three broad host-use categories: Opuntia specialists, columnar cactus specialists, and polymorphic species that use both host types. We recorded odor-evoked responses from all six maxillary palp OSN classes using single sensillum recordings and used electropalpograms to further evaluate species in which a pb2B-like class was not detected by single sensillum recordings (SSRs). The B-neuron classes clustered largely by OSN identity across species, retaining characteristic class-specific response profiles. The A-neuron classes were less clearly separated because of weak or overlapping response profiles. Despite these shared class-specific responses, species differed substantially in response magnitude and sensitivity to odorants. A pb2B-like class was not detected by SSR in D. mulleri, D. aldrichi, and D. straubae. Electropalpograms supported the absence or strong reduction of a phenol-responsive palpal signal in D. mulleri and D. straubae, while D. aldrichi retained a strong response. Principal component and phylogenetic principal component analyses did not reveal consistent clustering by host-use category. These results suggest that maxillary palp olfaction has evolved in a species- or lineage-specific manner rather than through a repeated host-category-specific shift in peripheral sensitivity.

artigo_base.titulo: The EF1A2-PABP-E75 axis coordinates metabolic reprogramming and 20E-dependent reproduction in mosquitoes
artigo_base.resumo_analitico: O artigo demonstra que o repasto sanguíneo deflagra uma cascata de reprogramação transcricional e energética via ecdisona (20E) e o complexo EF1A2-PABP-E75, desviando pools de aminoácidos e lipídios para a ovogênese enquanto reconfigura transitoriamente a homeostase oxidativa e a tolerância imunológica no epitélio intestinal.

ensaio.analise_ampla:
Por quase um século, a interação entre mosquitos vetores e patógenos como Plasmodium e arbovírus foi interpretada sob uma ótica estritamente imunocida: o mosquito reconheceria o invasor por receptores de padrões moleculares (PAMPs), ativaria as vias clássicas (Toll, Imd, JAK-STAT) e liberaria efetores líticos como defensinas e cecropinas. Essa visão simplista, contudo, ignorava o custo energético astronômico que o repasto sanguíneo e a digestão de hemo impõem ao vetor.

As publicações mais recentes da literatura internacional convergiram para um novo paradigma: a **competência vetorial não é apenas um estado imunológico, mas um desfecho metabólico**. A digestão do sangue força o intestino médio e o corpo gorduroso a operarem sob estresse oxidativo severo e excesso de lipídios, ativando vias de tolerância ao dano. É exatamente nessa janela fisiológica de reprogramação metabólica que os oocinetos de Plasmodium ou as partículas de DENV/ZIKV navegam entre os enterócitos.

### Diálogo com as Publicações e Histórico do LUCHM
O laboratório do Prof. Fábio Gomes (LUCHM/IBCCF/UFRJ) vem apontando para essa conexão multifatorial há mais de duas décadas:
1. **Polifosfatos e Bioenergética Celular:** Os trabalhos pioneiros do grupo sobre polifosfato inorgânico (polyP) e acidocalcisomas em protozoários e células de insetos demonstraram que reservas condensadas de fósforo e cátions são fundamentais não apenas como depósito estático, mas como 'baterias' dinâmicas de energia e moduladores de osmolaridade durante choques ambientais e de infecção.
2. **O Modelo Murino HFHS e a Dieta do Hospedeiro:** A investigação no LUCHM do repasto sanguíneo derivado de camundongos sob dieta hiperlipídica (HFHS) em modelos de malária experimental (PbA) revelou que a composição do sangue ingerido remodela os níveis de lipídios bioativos e a microbiota do mosquito, alterando a permeabilidade intestinal antes mesmo que o parasito atravesse a lâmina basal.
3. **Imune Priming e Epigenética:** A linha recente do grupo explorando marcas de histonas e memórias imunes (ontogenéticas e transgeracionais) em *Aedes* e *Anticarsia* reforça que o estado metabólico do inseto na fase larval ou em ciclos gonadotróficos prévios determina a sua reatividade contra desafios posteriores.

### Horizontes e Aplicações na Bancada
Essa mudança de perspectiva traz desdobramentos imediatos para os POPs do laboratório:
- **Calibração de Lotes:** A idade dos lotes de mosquitos e a dieta sacarina oferecida no insetário antes do repasto infectivo não são meras variáveis de manutenção, mas determinantes epigenéticos de reprodutibilidade experimental.
- **Leitura Contínua de Carga:** A substituição de dados binários de infecção (presença/ausência) por gradientes metabólicos e de carga viral (Ct contínuo de RT-qPCR) permite correlacionar o estresse fisiológico individual com a capacidade transmissora real na saliva.

temas_expansao.tema: Priming Imune Transgeracional & Epigenética da Cromatina em Insetos
temas_expansao.por_que_importa: Demonstra que invertebrados possuem mecanismos de memória imune adaptativa-símile mediados por remodelamento de cromatina (metilação de H3K27, acetilação de H4 e RNAs longos não-codificantes), capazes de persistir por gerações.
temas_expansao.fronteira: Mapear como a exposição prévia da larva a bactérias ou bioinseticidas (como Bacillus thuringiensis em Anticarsia) altera permanentemente a cromatina no intestino adulto, conferindo tolerância cruzada ou hiper-reatividade.
temas_expansao.gancho_luchm: Alimenta diretamente o projeto do mini-review da Frontiers in Immunology e a tese de doutorado sobre priming em mosquitos e lepidópteros.

temas_expansao.tema: O Eixo Imunometabólico Sangue–Intestino–Cérebro em Vetores
temas_expansao.por_que_importa: O repasto sanguíneo não apenas alimenta a ovogênese, mas dispara peptídeos enteroendócrinos e sinais neurais (como tachykininas e CCHa2) que comunicam o intestino ao cérebro do mosquito, alterando a locomoção, atração pelo hospedeiro e ciclo vigília-sono.
temas_expansao.fronteira: Investigar se a infecção por arbovírus (ZIKV, DENV) sequestra esses circuitos neuropeptídicos centrais para hiperativar o comportamento de picada e acelerar a disseminação viral na comunidade.
temas_expansao.gancho_luchm: Conecta as frentes de neurobiologia de insetos, olfação/fonotaxia e biologia celular do vetor em uma única pergunta mecanística integrada.

tecnicas_emergentes.tecnica: Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume Correlativa (Cryo-FIB-SEM e SBF-SEM)
tecnicas_emergentes.o_que_resolve: Permite reconstruir em 3D blocos teciduais inteiros (micrômetros cúbicos a milímetros cúbicos) com resolução nanométrica contínua, eliminando a perda de seções e o artefato de reconstrução 2D convencional.
tecnicas_emergentes.aplicacao_bancada: Permite visualizar esporozoítos de Plasmodium interagindo simultaneamente com dezenas de células acinares da glândula salivar de Anopheles, mapeando pontos de fusão de membrana e vesículas secretoras em escala nativa.
tecnicas_emergentes.status_no_luchm: Linha em franca consolidação via cooperação com o CENABIO e plataformas de ultraestrutura multiusuário da UFRJ.

tecnicas_emergentes.tecnica: Espectrometria de Massa com Imagem Espacial (MALDI-MSI / Desi-MSI)
tecnicas_emergentes.o_que_resolve: Mapeia a distribuição bidimensional direta de metabólitos, lipídios bioativos e polifosfatos diretamente sobre fatias criostáticas de tecidos de insetos, sem necessitar de homogeneização ou anticorpos.
tecnicas_emergentes.aplicacao_bancada: Permite visualizar com precisão microscópica onde os lipídios do repasto sanguíneo e os intermediários de polyP se concentram no intestino médio antes e depois da invasão pelo oocineto.
tecnicas_emergentes.status_no_luchm: Oportunidade de expansão analítica em colaboração com os laboratórios de metabolômica e proteômica estrutural.
